name: Psalms
author: Many are attributed to David, with others to Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses, and unnamed authors.
date: Composed over many centuries, from the time of Moses to after the exile.
setting: Songs and prayers used in Israel’s worship and personal life.
genre: Hebrew poetry: praise, lament, thanksgiving, wisdom, and royal psalms.
theme: God is king, and his people can bring all their joy and sorrow to him.

outline.label: Introduction: the two ways and the anointed king
Psalms of the sons of Korah
Moses, refuge, and the Sabbath song

christInBook: The psalms speak of the Messiah throughout: the anointed king (2), the suffering servant (22), the shepherd (23), the priest-king (110), and the stone the builders rejected (118). Jesus said that everything written about him in the Psalms had to be fulfilled (Luke 24:44).
howToRead: Read one psalm at a time and ask what kind it is: praise, lament, thanksgiving, wisdom, or royal. Notice how laments usually move from complaint to trust. The psalms teach you how to pray when you do not know what to say.
